2. Credit Default: Regression and Classification

Author

Taeheon Kim

Credit-default prediction involves more than maximizing classification accuracy. A useful empirical analysis must distinguish which characteristics carry predictive information, how regularization changes the fitted model, and how a decision threshold trades missed defaults against false alarms. This study examines these questions using linear regression, penalized regression, logistic regression, and a constrained decision tree.

The dataset contains 30,000 credit-card clients and 23 explanatory variables. Repayment status, billing amounts, and past payments provide a natural setting for comparing parsimonious linear specifications with nonlinear decision rules. The underlying data are documented by the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients repository. The analysis uses the existing local data and saved notebook results; no new sample is introduced here.

NoteCentral finding

In the recorded evaluation, the decision tree has a higher ROC AUC than logistic regression (0.7632 versus 0.7241). At a threshold of 0.6, it also identifies a larger share of defaults, but produces more false positives. The relevant finding is a trade-off between detection and selectivity, rather than an unconditional ranking of the models.

Sections (a)–(d) establish the sample and linear benchmarks; (e)–(g) examine shrinkage; (h)–(j) evaluate logistic regression; and (k)–(n) investigate decision rules and compare the classifiers.

2.(a) Summary statistics

The target mean is the observed default share: 0.2212, or 6,636 clients. Class imbalance matters because a classifier can attain substantial accuracy while detecting very few defaults. The summary of PAY_AMT5 also shows why scaling is relevant: its standard deviation substantially exceeds its mean, so raw monetary magnitudes differ greatly from demographic and repayment-status codes.

Python implementation 
# (a)번: Y와 X22의 평균 및 표준편차 계산
y_mean = data['default payment next month'].mean()
y_std = data['default payment next month'].std()

x22_mean = data['PAY_AMT5'].mean()
x22_std = data['PAY_AMT5'].std()

# Default 관측치(Y=1)의 개수 계산
default_count = data[data['default payment next month'] == 1].shape[0]

# 결과 출력
print(f"Y 평균: {y_mean}, Y 표준편차: {y_std}")
print(f"X22 평균: {x22_mean}, X22 표준편차: {x22_std}")
print(f"Default 관측치 개수 (Y=1): {default_count}")

2.(b) Training and evaluation samples

The first 20,000 rows form the training sample and the remaining 10,000 form the evaluation sample. This is a row-based split; the notebook does not establish it as a chronological forecasting design. Standardization is fitted on the training predictors and applied to the evaluation predictors. The target remains unscaled.

This preserves a clear separation for scaling, but interpretation still depends on the original encoding of categorical variables. Numeric category codes enter the regressions as numbers rather than as a full set of indicator variables.

Python implementation 
# 컬럼 이름 확인
columns = data.columns

# 데이터셋 분리
train_data = data.iloc[:20000, :]
test_data = data.iloc[20000:, :]

# Z-Score 스케일링
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_train_scaled = pd.DataFrame(
    scaler.fit_transform(train_data.iloc[:, 1:-1]),  # X 변수만 스케일링
    columns=columns[1:-1]
)
X_test_scaled = pd.DataFrame(
    scaler.transform(test_data.iloc[:, 1:-1]),
    columns=columns[1:-1]
)


# 원래 Y는 스케일링하지 않음
train_y_mean = train_data['default payment next month'].mean()
train_y_std = train_data['default payment next month'].std()
test_y_mean = test_data['default payment next month'].mean()
test_y_std = test_data['default payment next month'].std()

# 훈련 세트와 테스트 세트의 X6 평균과 표준편차 계산
train_x6_mean = X_train_scaled['PAY_0'].mean()
train_x6_std = X_train_scaled['PAY_0'].std()
test_x6_mean = X_test_scaled['PAY_0'].mean()
test_x6_std = X_test_scaled['PAY_0'].std()

# 결과 출력
print(f"훈련 데이터 Y 평균: {train_y_mean}, 표준편차: {train_y_std}")
print(f"테스트 데이터 Y 평균: {test_y_mean}, 표준편차: {test_y_std}")
print(f"훈련 데이터 X6 평균: {train_x6_mean}, 표준편차: {train_x6_std}")
print(f"테스트 데이터 X6 평균: {test_x6_mean}, 표준편차: {test_x6_std}")

2.(c) Linear regression

An ordinary least-squares regression provides an interpretable benchmark for the binary outcome. Its role here is to summarize predictive associations and squared-error fit; its predictions are not constrained to be probabilities. The recorded adjusted R² is 0.12090, with training and evaluation MSEs of 0.15451 and 0.14409. The standardized PAY_0 coefficient is positive, about 0.10829, consistent with repayment status carrying predictive information about default.

Python implementation 
# Y는 스케일링하지 않음
y_train = train_data['default payment next month']
y_test = test_data['default payment next month']


# (c)번: statsmodels로 회귀 분석
# 상수항 추가
X_train_scaled_const = sm.add_constant(X_train_scaled)
X_test_scaled_const = sm.add_constant(X_test_scaled)

# 회귀 모델 학습
model = sm.OLS(y_train, X_train_scaled_const).fit()

# (1) X6의 계수
x6_coefficient = model.params['PAY_0']

# (2) Adjusted R^2
adjusted_r2_train = model.rsquared_adj

# (3) 10% 유의 수준에서 유의한 변수 개수
p_values = model.pvalues
significant_vars = (p_values < 0.1).sum()

# (4) 훈련 및 테스트 세트 MSE
y_train_pred = model.predict(X_train_scaled_const)
y_test_pred = model.predict(X_test_scaled_const)
mse_train = mean_squared_error(y_train, y_train_pred)
mse_test = mean_squared_error(y_test, y_test_pred)

# 결과 출력
print(f"X6의 계수: {x6_coefficient}")
print(f"Adjusted R^2 (훈련 세트): {adjusted_r2_train}")
print(f"10% 유의 수준에서 유의한 변수 개수: {significant_vars}")
print(f"훈련 세트 MSE: {mse_train}")
print(f"테스트 세트 MSE: {mse_test}")
X6의 계수: 0.10829073719372384
Adjusted R^2 (훈련 세트): 0.12090017221466631
10% 유의 수준에서 유의한 변수 개수: 13
훈련 세트 MSE: 0.15450990359685435

2.(d) Variable selection and model comparison

The next specification retains variables significant at the 10% level in the original linear fit. This examines whether a smaller model can retain comparable predictive fit. The PAY_0 coefficient changes only slightly, from 0.10829 to 0.10897, while evaluation MSE changes from 0.144089 to 0.143929. The difference is small; without uncertainty estimates, it supports a descriptive comparison rather than a statistically established performance gain.

Python implementation 
# (1) 10% 유의 수준에서 유의한 변수 선택
significant_columns = p_values[p_values < 0.1].index  # 10% 유의 수준의 변수들
X_train_significant = X_train_scaled_const[significant_columns]
X_test_significant = X_test_scaled_const[significant_columns]

# (2) 선택된 변수로 회귀 모델 학습
model_significant = sm.OLS(y_train, X_train_significant).fit()

# (3) X6의 계수 (PAY_0)
x6_coefficient_d = model_significant.params['PAY_0']

# (4) Adjusted R^2 계산
adjusted_r2_train_d = model_significant.rsquared_adj

# (5) 훈련 및 테스트 세트 MSE
y_train_pred_d = model_significant.predict(X_train_significant)
y_test_pred_d = model_significant.predict(X_test_significant)
mse_train_d = mean_squared_error(y_train, y_train_pred_d)
mse_test_d = mean_squared_error(y_test, y_test_pred_d)

# 결과 출력
print(f"(d) 선택된 변수만 사용한 회귀 분석 결과:")
print(f"X6의 계수 (PAY_0): {x6_coefficient_d}")
print(f"Adjusted R^2 (훈련 세트): {adjusted_r2_train_d}")
print(f"훈련 세트 MSE: {mse_train_d}")
print(f"테스트 세트 MSE: {mse_test_d}")
(d) 선택된 변수만 사용한 회귀 분석 결과:
X6의 계수 (PAY_0): 0.10896820264679041
Adjusted R^2 (훈련 세트): 0.12079599739653435
훈련 세트 MSE: 0.1546133059105144

2.(e) Ridge regularization

Ridge regression penalizes the squared coefficient norm, trading some in-sample fit for a less variable specification. The curve below examines 50 penalty values between 500 and 2,500. The recorded model at λ = 1,300 has evaluation MSE 0.143944 and a PAY_0 coefficient of 0.09815.

Read the vertical-axis offset carefully: the visible U-shape represents a narrow range of MSE differences. Because the evaluation sample is used to inspect the penalty curve, this score is not an untouched final-test estimate following tuning.

Python implementation 
# λ 값 설정 (500 ~ 2500 사이 50개)
lambdas = np.linspace(500, 2500, 50)

# Ridge 회귀를 수행하고 MSE 저장
train_mse = []
test_mse = []

for lam in lambdas:
    ridge = Ridge(alpha=lam)  # λ 값을 alpha로 설정
    ridge.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    y_train_pred = ridge.predict(X_train_scaled)
    y_test_pred = ridge.predict(X_test_scaled)
    train_mse.append(mean_squared_error(y_train, y_train_pred))
    test_mse.append(mean_squared_error(y_test, y_test_pred))

# λ = 1300에서의 결과
ridge_1300 = Ridge(alpha=1300)
ridge_1300.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
y_train_pred_1300 = ridge_1300.predict(X_train_scaled)
y_test_pred_1300 = ridge_1300.predict(X_test_scaled)

mse_train_1300 = mean_squared_error(y_train, y_train_pred_1300)
mse_test_1300 = mean_squared_error(y_test, y_test_pred_1300)
x6_coefficient_1300 = ridge_1300.coef_[X_train_scaled.columns.get_loc('PAY_0')]

# 결과 출력
print(f"λ=1300일 때 훈련 세트 MSE: {mse_train_1300}")
print(f"λ=1300일 때 테스트 세트 MSE: {mse_test_1300}")
print(f"λ=1300일 때 X6의 계수 (PAY_0): {x6_coefficient_1300}")

# λ 값에 따른 테스트 세트 MSE 시각화
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(lambdas, test_mse, label="Test MSE", color='blue', linewidth=2)
plt.xlabel("Lambda")
plt.ylabel("MSE")
plt.title("Ridge Regression")
plt.legend()
plt.grid()
plt.show()
λ=1300일 때 훈련 세트 MSE: 0.1546220114558191
λ=1300일 때 테스트 세트 MSE: 0.1439435634389618
λ=1300일 때 X6의 계수 (PAY_0): 0.09815247232625099

2.(f) Lasso regularization and coefficients

Lasso uses an absolute-value penalty and can set coefficients exactly to zero. In the recorded fit at λ = 0.0017, 15 of the 23 predictor coefficients remain nonzero, and evaluation MSE is 0.143913. The coefficient table is therefore useful for examining sparsity as well as prediction.

A zero coefficient indicates exclusion under this fitted penalty and sample; it does not prove that a characteristic is economically irrelevant. In particular, correlated billing and payment measures can substitute for one another. Ridge and Lasso penalty values also use different objective scalings, so their numerical magnitudes should not be compared directly.

Python implementation 
# λ 값 생성 (0.001 ~ 0.003 사이 50개)
lambdas = np.linspace(0.001, 0.003, 50)

# Lasso 회귀 수행 및 MSE 저장
train_mse = []
test_mse = []

for lam in lambdas:
    lasso = Lasso(alpha=lam)  # λ 값을 alpha로 설정
    lasso.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    y_train_pred = lasso.predict(X_train_scaled)
    y_test_pred = lasso.predict(X_test_scaled)
    train_mse.append(mean_squared_error(y_train, y_train_pred))
    test_mse.append(mean_squared_error(y_test, y_test_pred))

# λ = 0.0017에서의 결과
lambda_0017 = 0.0017
lasso_0017 = Lasso(alpha=lambda_0017)
lasso_0017.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)

# 예측 및 MSE 계산
y_train_pred_0017 = lasso_0017.predict(X_train_scaled)
y_test_pred_0017 = lasso_0017.predict(X_test_scaled)
mse_train_0017 = mean_squared_error(y_train, y_train_pred_0017)
mse_test_0017 = mean_squared_error(y_test, y_test_pred_0017)

# X6의 회귀 계수 및 비영 계수 개수
x6_coefficient_0017 = lasso_0017.coef_[X_train_scaled.columns.get_loc('PAY_0')]
nonzero_coefficients = np.sum(lasso_0017.coef_ != 0)

# 결과 출력
print(f"λ=0.0017일 때 훈련 세트 MSE: {mse_train_0017}")
print(f"λ=0.0017일 때 테스트 세트 MSE: {mse_test_0017}")
print(f"λ=0.0017일 때 X6의 계수 (PAY_0): {x6_coefficient_0017}")
print(f"λ=0.0017일 때 비영 계수 개수: {nonzero_coefficients}")

# λ 값에 따른 MSE 시각화
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(lambdas, test_mse, label="Test MSE", linewidth=2)
plt.xlabel("Lambda")
plt.ylabel("MSE")
plt.title("Lasso Regression")
plt.legend()
plt.grid()
plt.show()

λ=0.0017일 때 테스트 세트 MSE: 0.1439128159405255
λ=0.0017일 때 X6의 계수 (PAY_0): 0.10791813237228776

2.(g) Elastic Net

Elastic Net combines L1 and L2 penalties. The evaluated specification uses alpha=1300 and l1_ratio=0.0017 and produces evaluation MSE 0.165023, worse than the other recorded regression fits. Reusing the numerical settings of the preceding Ridge and Lasso exercises does not construct an optimally tuned Elastic Net: l1_ratio is a mixing proportion, not an independently selected Lasso penalty. This result concerns that particular specification.

Python implementation 
# Elastic Net 설정: alpha = 1300, l1_ratio = 0.0017
elastic_net = ElasticNet(alpha=1300, l1_ratio=0.0017)
elastic_net.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)

# 훈련 및 테스트 예측
y_train_pred = elastic_net.predict(X_train_scaled)
y_test_pred = elastic_net.predict(X_test_scaled)

# MSE 계산
mse_train = mean_squared_error(y_train, y_train_pred)
mse_test = mean_squared_error(y_test, y_test_pred)

# 결과 출력
print(f"Elastic Net (alpha=1300, l1_ratio=0.0017):")
print(f"훈련 세트 MSE: {mse_train}")
print(f"테스트 세트 MSE: {mse_test}")

2.(h) Logistic regression

Logistic regression models the log-odds of default and produces scores in [0, 1]. The notebook fits a scikit-learn specification for prediction and a statsmodels specification for additional model summaries. These are related but distinct fits. The reported statsmodels pseudo R² is 0.1165 and the PAY_0 coefficient is approximately 0.6407. A pseudo R² is not directly comparable to the adjusted R² from ordinary least squares.

Python implementation 
# Logistic Regression 모델 학습
logistic_model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)
logistic_model.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)

print(logistic_model.intercept_, logistic_model.coef_)

# 상수항 추가
X_train_const = sm.add_constant(X_train_scaled)
X_test_const = sm.add_constant(X_test_scaled)

# 로지스틱 회귀 모델 학습
logit_model = sm.Logit(y_train, X_train_const).fit()

# Pseudo R2 계산
pseudo_r2 = 1 - (logit_model.llf / logit_model.llnull)

2.(i) Logistic classification thresholds

A predicted probability becomes a classification only after choosing a threshold. At 0.6, logistic regression has accuracy 0.8058 but recall of only 0.09384: fewer than one in ten observed defaults are identified. Raising the threshold to 0.8 reduces recall to 0.01732. High specificity and acceptable overall accuracy therefore coexist with weak default detection at these thresholds.

Python implementation 
y_test_proba = logistic_model.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]

# Threshold 리스트
thresholds = [0.6, 0.7, 0.8]

# 결과 저장을 위한 리스트
results_list = []

# 반복문으로 각 Threshold별 계산
for threshold in thresholds:
    # Threshold 적용
    preds = np.where(y_test_proba > threshold, 1, 0)

    # 혼동 행렬 계산
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, preds)
    TP = cm[1, 1]  # True Positive
    FN = cm[1, 0]  # False Negative
    FP = cm[0, 1]  # False Positive
    TN = cm[0, 0]  # True Negative

    # 평가 지표 계산
    accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, preds)
    tpr = recall_score(y_test, preds)  # True Positive Rate (Recall)
    tnr = TN / (TN + FP)  # True Negative Rate (Specificity)
    fpr = FP / (FP + TN)  # False Positive Rate
    precision = precision_score(y_test, preds)
    f1 = f1_score(y_test, preds)

    # 결과 저장
    results_list.append({
        "Threshold": threshold,
        "Accuracy": accuracy,
        "True Positive Rate": tpr,
        "True Negative Rate": tnr,
        "False Positive Rate": fpr,
        "Precision": precision,
        "F1-Score": f1
    })

# 리스트를 DataFrame으로 변환
results_df = pd.DataFrame(results_list)

results_df.T

2.(j) Logistic ROC analysis

The ROC curve varies the decision threshold and plots the true-positive rate against the false-positive rate. The recorded AUC of 0.72410 summarizes ranking discrimination over thresholds. It does not establish that predicted probabilities are calibrated, nor does it determine which threshold is appropriate for a particular loss function.

lr_auc=roc_auc_score(y_test,lr_prob)

2.(k) Decision tree and visualization

The decision tree allows nonlinear thresholds and interactions without imposing a single additive log-odds equation. Complexity is limited by a maximum depth of five and a minimum of 500 observations per leaf. The visible tree is part of the empirical argument: its root split uses PAY_0, and subsequent branches show how repayment history and payment amounts combine.

Training and evaluation accuracy are 0.8128 and 0.8331. The largest impurity-based importance is assigned to PAY_0 (0.6762), followed by PAY_2 and PAY_AMT2. These importance values describe this tree’s splits; they are not causal effects or universally comparable measures of economic importance. The plotted split values are on the standardized feature scale.

Python implementation 
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from sklearn.tree import plot_tree

# Decision Tree Model Specification
decision_tree = DecisionTreeClassifier(
    criterion="entropy",
    min_samples_split=100,
    min_samples_leaf=500,
    max_depth=5,
    random_state=42
)

# Fit the Decision Tree Model
decision_tree.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)

# Predict and Evaluate Model
y_train_pred = decision_tree.predict(X_train_scaled)
y_test_pred = decision_tree.predict(X_test_scaled)

train_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_train, y_train_pred)
test_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, y_test_pred)

# Feature Importance
feature_importance = pd.DataFrame({
    "Feature": X_train_scaled.columns,
    "Importance": decision_tree.feature_importances_
}).sort_values(by="Importance", ascending=False)

# Select Top 3 Features
top_3_features = feature_importance.head(3)

# Results Output
print(f"Training Accuracy: {train_accuracy:.4f}")
print(f"Testing Accuracy: {test_accuracy:.4f}")
print("\nTop 3 Important Features:")
print(top_3_features)

# Plot the Decision Tree
plt.figure(figsize=(20, 10))  # Adjust the size as needed
plot_tree(
    decision_tree,
    feature_names=X_train_scaled.columns,
    class_names=["No Default", "Default"],
    filled=True,
    rounded=True,
    fontsize=10,
    max_depth=5  # To match the maximum depth of the tree
)
plt.title("Decision Tree Visualization")
plt.show()

2.(m) Tree ROC analysis

The tree’s AUC is 0.76319, approximately 0.0391 above the logistic model in this sample. The coarse ROC shape is consistent with the limited set of scores produced by terminal leaves. The difference is descriptive: the notebook does not report resampling uncertainty or a paired significance test for the AUC gap.

2.(n) Comparative interpretation

The evidence can be summarized at a common decision threshold without obscuring the different error profiles.

Metric Logistic regression Constrained tree
ROC AUC 0.72410 0.76319
Recall at 0.6 0.09384 0.25457
False-positive rate at 0.6 0.00745 0.02411
Precision at 0.6 0.76772 0.73472
F1 at 0.6 0.16724 0.37813

The tree offers better default detection at the cost of more false alarms. Selecting a model for a lending decision would require an explicit treatment of error costs, calibration, and the information available when the decision is made. Those decision-specific analyses are not supplied by accuracy or AUC alone.

Discussion and research implications

The regression sequence shows that sparsity can be obtained with little change in the observed squared-error fit. The classification sequence shows that model choice and threshold choice answer different questions. The tree’s higher AUC is informative, but its practical interpretation requires the false-positive and false-negative consequences to be specified.

The analysis does not identify causal effects of borrower characteristics. It also does not establish robust superiority across samples: the regularization curves reuse the evaluation set, category codes impose numerical structure, and uncertainty around performance differences is not estimated. A stronger continuation would fit all preprocessing inside a validation pipeline, tune penalties on a validation sample, and reserve a final sample for discrimination and calibration assessment. Cost-sensitive threshold evaluation would then connect the statistical comparison to a clearly stated decision problem.

Research reproducibility and source documentation.
